title: Acknowledge composer sends at once and keep their ownership across remounts and reconnects
prompt:
Sending a message from the chat composer to a session served by the detached runtime shows nothing until the runtime answers, and pressing Enter again in that gap sends twice. The composer should acknowledge a send at once: show that it is sending, refuse a second submission while one is pending, and when the send settles keep whatever the person typed or attached in the meantime. The draft is cleared only if it is still exactly the submitted text and nobody touched it during the send.

That pending state cannot live inside the Composer component. Switching tabs or collapsing the panel remounts the composer, and a refusal that arrives while no composer is mounted must still be shown when it comes back. So the pending send and its failure belong to a module-level store, src/lib/composerSends.ts, that Composer (src/components/chat/Composer.tsx) and TabView (src/components/session/TabView.tsx) both read. The store is keyed by where the message goes. A cloud session's live connection is replaced on every reconnect (its `generation` changes), but a send issued before the reconnect still belongs to the same mailbox, so the key must name the destination, not the connection.

Other code and tests use this interface of src/lib/composerSends.ts:
- `beginComposerSend(key: string, tabId: string): ComposerSend | null` starts a send for `key` and returns null when one is already pending for that key. Starting a send clears any failure retained for the key. Keys are independent of each other.
- A `ComposerSend` has `ownsDraft(): boolean`. It is true only while the tab's draft (`getDraft`/`setDraft` in src/lib/drafts.ts) has not changed since the send began. Any `setDraft` for that tab after the send began, even one that writes the same text, means the send no longer owns the draft.
- `editComposerSend(key: string)` marks the pending send for `key` as edited.
- `finishComposerSend(key: string, operation: ComposerSend, error?: unknown)` settles the send. It does nothing when `operation` is not the key's current pending send, so a late, stale settlement cannot clear a newer send. With an error, the error is kept for the key.
- `clearComposerSendError(key: string)` drops the kept error (an explicit recovery).
- `useComposerSend(key: string)` is a React hook returning `{ pending: ComposerSend | null, error: unknown | null }`. It updates its subscribers, and the state is kept while nobody subscribes, so a remounted view sees the same pending send or error.
- `composerSendScope(backend: { kind: string; key: string; logSessionId: string }, tabId: string): string` builds the key. Two backends that differ only in other fields, such as `generation`, give the same key. A different `kind`, `key`, `logSessionId` or tab gives a different key.

Keep the existing composer history behaviour: settling a send consumes only the submitted history entry, so a newer history browse keeps its saved draft.
notes:
Source: PR #649, four commits; the fourth only edits CHANGELOG.md.
Chain: 0ec69de6 adds pending-send refs (sendPending, draftRevision) inside Composer.tsx and the acknowledgement in TabView.tsx. 4933c328 moves exactly that state out of Composer.tsx into the new src/lib/composerSends.ts (beginComposerSend, finishComposerSend, useComposerSend, editComposerSend) and has TabView.tsx key it by a sendScope built from backend.kind/key/generation and tab id. 9d79045a replaces that generation-based sendScope with composerSendScope() added to composerSends.ts, so a send keeps its owner across cloud reconnects.
Each step reworks what the one before it introduced: there is no store to scope until the refs move out of the component, and nothing to move until the refs exist.
The check runs the store's unit test, which the PR added and which covers the second and third steps. The PR's UI tests (Composer.test.tsx, TabView.history.test.tsx) depend on exact labels and are left out.
